about: Clay's head as fitted architectural pieces (see head_sheets.md): an orange face mass, a dark roof shell fitted over it whose back corners continue as the horns, a nose crest on the front of the roof, a hinged jaw, eyes with lids hinged on the canthal axis, and ear frills tucked under the horns. Model units: z = (700 - px) / 343, y = (830 - py) / 343, from the 1400 px side reference; x = Clay's left.

upper_head.note: The orange face mass under the roof. Upper lip line, traced on the side sheet (orange face over cream jaw) and the same in How to Draw and the flight render: from the bottom of the nose it slopes down and back, an overhanging lip that is lowest about a third of the way back (z 1.85); from there it rises in a long, slightly concave line to below the eye, then turns sharply up at the mouth corner (z 1.59) and runs back, gently rising, to the ear opening (z 1.41, y 1.656), where it curls up into the cheek's back edge (anatomy: back edge of the cheek). Traced on the centre of the drawn line. The muzzle hardly narrows toward the front and has near-vertical sides, but it has no flat front wall: its top comes down to meet the front of the upper jaw (the lip), so the roof runs all the way down to the front of the upper jaw, and the nose comes out of the roof's front.
upper_head.ridge_note: The roof is a gable: two mirrored slopes falling from a crisp ridge down its whole length; the ridge is on the measured top profile and the shoulders drop below it (rows: z, drop at the shoulders). The plates are mirrored pairs meeting at the ridge.

front.note: The front muzzle of the upper jaw, in front of the bite point (z 1.86): below the nose its front face is convex (the side sheet's notch at z 1.98 is the nose's underside, not a hollow in the face), then its underside sweeps back and down to the bite point, where it meets the lower jaw's front. That underside is skin, with no teeth. Its bottom corners pull up a little before angling round to the side muzzle. A small brown ridge (the roof's front edge) wraps across the top of the front face right under the nose. From above the front face is rounded across (convex: its middle 0.025 forward of its sides; the roof's front band follows the same curve, so the front ridge runs on from it flush) and bulges forward in side profile (0.01, side sheet front outline), and the front ridge's front edge follows that curve. Its bottom edge, the front lip edge, arcs down in the middle (0.03 lower than at the corners).

ridge.note: The front ridge (circled by the user on the flight render): a subtle extension of the roof's front. The roof's front band is one simple piece, not a mirrored pair: it wraps over the ridge down to the eave and carries on, with no edge, down over the front of the snout under the nose. Its only edge there is its bottom, where it meets the orange front muzzle (eave_y), which follows the front's convex curve, rolling over in a quarter round. Side sheet: the brown-to-orange line at the front sits at about 1.356-1.363 (z 1.99-1.95); the ridge's bottom edge and the plates beside it meet at 1.37, so they form one line and a band of orange front muzzle shows below, as in the flight render.

lower_jaw.note: A separate piece from the neck, on its own hinge; traced on the side sheet. Set back under the overhanging upper lip (strong overbite): its chin is a short point at z 1.86, right under the lowest point of the lip. Its underside drops back to its lowest at z 1.77, then rises to the throat notch (z 1.60), where the neck begins. From there its back edge is the heavy line that runs back and up along the neck (z 1.55, y 1.41; z 1.44, y 1.46) and turns up into the ear opening (z 1.39). Its top edge runs just inside the upper lip line at the front and just above it (hidden inside the cheek) behind the mouth corner. At the back it is as wide as the cheek (the jowl), so it stands proud of the neck and its back edge reads as a step, not a seam. Skin: cream with faint pebble scales, like the face's but larger and softer; the neck's transverse bands start below its back edge. Its front is as wide as the upper jaw's mouth at the bite point, so the two fronts meet across the bite when the mouth is closed.

dark_plate_edge.note: The roof's lower edge, traced on the side sheet's colour boundary (dark roof over orange face) and checked against How to Draw and the flight render, which agree on its shape: the roof covers the whole nose, down to the lip at the front; from the nose the edge rises only gently for the front third of the muzzle, then turns sharply up in a near-vertical step at about mid-muzzle, climbs steeply and diagonally to the front of the eye, runs over the top of the eye (the eye tucked right under it), steps up again behind the eye and runs back toward the ear. The rim plates (edge row) follow this line.

eye.note: Round, wide-open eye tucked under the eave. Measured on a line map of the side sheet (eye centre px 120, py 250): the inner (medial) corner runs down and forward into a point, with the pink tear duct, about 58 degrees below horizontal from the centre and well out from the round eye; the outer (lateral) corner sits about 32 degrees above horizontal toward the back. So the canthal axis rises about 45 degrees toward the back and is bent, each corner turned 13 degrees further down. The inner corner is rounded and holds the caruncle; the outer closes to a point. The upper margin arcs highest a little toward the inner corner; the lower margin dips lowest toward the outer corner. The lids are thick shells with a rounded margin, hinged on the canthal axis.

lids.columns_note: outer/inner_canthus_deg: where the corners sit on the eyeball, measured from the gaze along the canthal axis. open_deg: how far the margin opens from the gaze at mid-eye; skew tilts where it peaks (negative = toward the inner corner); corner_exp near 0.5 keeps the corner rounded, 1 or more closes it to a point.

caruncle.note: Not a bead: a small fleshy teardrop filling the inner corner between the two lid margins, lying on the eyeball, its point toward the corner, its round end toward the iris; pink, partly tucked under the lids.

lids.blink_note: Each lid turns about the canthal axis, so its margin travels across the eye at right angles to the line between the corners; the lids meet along that line, a little below mid-eye (the upper lid does the moving). Stored as 6 in-between shapes along the arc so the lid stays on the eyeball's surface all the way down.

socket.note: The face is carved into a socket that holds the eye assembly: inside the lids' footprint the skin runs in just under the lid dome, and a rounded rim (the orbital rim under the lid-ring muscle) turns it back out to the face.

eye.round_note: Every official image shows a round eye: the opening nearly a circle (the lids open 48 and 50 degrees, corners at the measured 42 and 60 degrees from the gaze, rounded), a white ring round a large dark-brown iris and pupil, a heavy dark ring round the whole opening, and the pink tear duct at the lower front corner. The lids hug the eyeball (thickness 0.05 r), so there is no dome.
eye.inner_note: Every image: the inner (front) corner drops below the round eye into a pointed teardrop holding the pink tear duct. So the inner corner sits further round the eyeball (72 degrees), turns further down (20-degree bend; 26 or more twists the lower lid through the face) and closes to a point (corner exponent 1.1).

horn.note: The horn grows out of the roof: its root is sculpted into the roof plates, which swell up and wrap its base (a smooth union with fillet radius `fillet`), so the roof's top line runs on into the horn's top line. From there it sweeps back and up in a long, nearly straight line, tapering slowly, and curls up only in the last stretch. Smooth, with hairline incised rings.

ear_frill.note: Measured on the side sheet (frill crop, px 205-262, py 188-224): an almond leaf about 0.18 long and 0.06 wide, from its base at the back of the cheek (front-lower end) back and up to its tip under the horn. It lies close along the side of the head, its face turned outward (the side sheet shows its whole face), cupped like a horse's ear laid back: pale peach hollow inside, an orange rim, the top edge rolled out and over. Its top edge runs back under the horn.

roof.note: A thin dark underlay fitted over the face; the visible roof is the plates laid on it (roof_plates). Its eave line is dark_plate_edge.

nose_crest.note: Superseded by 'nose': the nose is its own piece. Only the front pad remains, off (height 0).

anatomy.note: Sculpt from the inside out: bone landmarks first, muscle masses over them, then skin creases where muscles meet or skin folds over something that moves. Every entry says what it is and what it does to the surface. Positions are side-view (z, y); offsets act on the side of the face.

bone.name: cheekbone (the line under the eye)
bone.why: Clay's cheekbone is the heavy hooked line under the eye in every reference, measured here from the side sheet: it starts thin below the front of the eye, runs back under it (heaviest beneath the back of the eye), turns up steeply at a corner behind and below the eye, then sweeps back and tapers out. It is the rim of the eye socket: a raised ridge cupping the eye from below and behind, sloping gently up toward the eye and dropping crisply on the outside, where the line is drawn. Sculpted, not drawn.

bone.name: eye socket
bone.why: The bony orbit between brow, cheekbone and postorbital bar. Eye and fat fill it; the surface only seats slightly so the lids stand clear of the face round the opening.

bone.name: back edge of the cheek, curling into the ear
bone.why: Side sheet: the heavy mouth line runs back and up to the ear opening, then does not stop: it curls up and forward round the opening and climbs to the base of the ear frill, so the cheek's back edge becomes the ear. The neck's orange continues behind it, so this is a form edge, not a colour edge: a raised rim, sloping gently into the cheek in front and dropping crisply behind, where the line is drawn.

muscle.name: orbicularis (lid ring)
muscle.why: The ring muscle round the eye that closes it: a soft raised ring framing the lids, inside the cheekbone rim. (No form raises the skin inside eye.clear_radius, where the lids sit.)

muscle.name: masseter
muscle.why: The jaw-closing muscle from the zygomatic arch down to the jaw: the full rounded cheek above the cream jowl, behind the mouth corner.

muscle.name: lip and snout muscle (levator)
muscle.why: Lifts the upper lip; a gentle fullness on the side of the muzzle in front of the eye, below the roof's eave.

muscle.name: temporalis
muscle.why: Fills the skull behind the eye up to the roof; it is why the cranium under the roof is wide behind the brow. Shaped by the face stations, not a brush.

skin.name: masseter fold over the jowl
skin.why: The cheek muscle's lower edge folding over the jowl, parallel to and above the rising mouth line.

skin.name: ear opening
skin.why: The ear opening, where the mouth line ends and turns up into the cheek's back edge.

skin.name: pit at the eave notch in front of the eye
skin.why: A small pit at the corner of the rim's step in front of the eye (side sheet); not the nostril.

expressions.note: Expression comes from muscles. Each muscle action is a shape of the face (a morph target) plus lid bone turns; an expression is a mix of actions, after the Facial Action Coding System (FACS action units noted). Clay's brow is the rigid roof eave, so brow actions move the skin between eave and lid, and the lids, rather than the plate.

cheekRaise.muscles: orbicularis oculi, orbital part, with zygomaticus major pulling the mouth corner up and back

lipRaise.muscles: levator labii superioris (and alaeque nasi): lifts the upper lip off the teeth and wrinkles the snout

lipCornerDown.muscles: depressor anguli oris: pulls the mouth corner down

browLower.muscles: corrugator and procerus: draw the brow skin down and in toward the inner corner; the skin between eave and upper lid bunches over the eye

innerBrowRaise.muscles: frontalis, inner part: lifts the skin above the inner corner of the eye

expressions.pose_columns: lids: turns in radians of [upper lid inner half, upper lid outer half, lower lid]; positive closes
expressions.muscle_actions_note: blink (orbicularis oculi, palpebral part: AU45) is a shape of the lids themselves, built with them

roof_plates.note: The roof in pieces of one kind: bands of tiles from the roof's flat front edge back, each band a mirrored pair meeting at the ridge, a rim of square marginal scutes along the eave, and one tile over the flat front face (the nose comes out of it). Every tile is a solid of even thickness with a short wall and a narrow chamfer at its edges; the gaps between them are the drawn lines. Laid out in profile coordinates: s along the top profile from the front edge back, d the depth below it; joints are lines of constant s.

rows.name: edge row
rows.note: the rim of the roof: square marginal scutes like a turtle shell's edge, thicker than the plates above, their lower edges rolled outward; each one's lower edge steps with the stepped dark_plate_edge

front_plate.note: A plate over the flat front face of the box muzzle, from the top edge down to the eave, above the orange lip band that wraps round the front.

nose.note: The nose is one extruded mass, its section like the border of the Superman shield: a flat top with square corners, short sides falling straight down, then two lower edges converging to a point. It comes out of the front of the roof, which slopes down to the front of the upper jaw, its axis level so its front face aims straight forward; organically softened: rounded corners, softly convex faces and a rounded rim round the front face; its back is buried in the snout. Side sheet: its top front corner is the nose tip, about (2.02-2.03, 1.443). The nostrils are slits in its two lower faces (the undersides), near the front.

nostril.note: t: distance along the nose's axis from the front face (negative = back); across: position across each lower face (0 = keel, 1 = outer edge); half_width in those units

nose.pitch_note: its axis follows the roof's top at the front, falling 43 degrees toward the tip (side sheet: from (1.95, 1.517) to the tip (2.012, 1.459)), so its top surface is the roof's top surface carried on: it emerges from it smoothly (its back dips under the roof) and juts out at the tip.
nose.size_note: side sheet front outline: the tip juts furthest at y 1.44 (z 2.019); just under it a notch at y 1.414 (z 1.98) where the nose's underside meets the front of the upper jaw, which carries on down to the lip at z 2.0-2.01

teeth.note: Flight render and limited edition: small, flat, triangular blades. The tooth rows start at the bite point (z 1.86), where the upper and lower fronts of the mouth meet when it is closed: a short row across the front of the mouth there, then rows back along each side lip, each tooth perpendicular to its lip edge, tips raked a little back. In front of the bite point is the front muzzle's underside: skin, no teeth. A little larger mid-row; no single big fang.
